Description: An introduction to the psychological principles underlying education, exploring how students learn, develop, and are motivated in educational settings. Emphasis is placed on applying theory to classroom practice within the Zambian context.
LearningOutcomes: Explain key psychological theories and their application in educational settings
Analyse factors that influence student motivation and learning behaviour
Apply psychological principles to design effective teaching strategies

Description: A comprehensive study of curriculum theory and design, examining models for developing, implementing, and evaluating educational curricula at various levels. Students explore national curriculum frameworks and contextualise them for Zambian schools.
LearningOutcomes: Design curriculum frameworks aligned with national educational standards
Evaluate existing curricula using recognised assessment models
Develop learning objectives and assessment criteria for diverse learner groups

Description: An advanced exploration of instructional strategies and pedagogical approaches, equipping student teachers with diverse methods to facilitate effective learning in varied classroom environments. Includes microteaching and reflective practice components.
LearningOutcomes: Apply a range of evidence-based teaching methods appropriate to different learning contexts
Develop lesson plans that accommodate diverse learning styles and abilities
Critically evaluate pedagogical approaches and reflect on personal teaching practice

Description: An introductory course covering essential communication skills in business contexts, including written, oral, and digital communication for professional and organisational settings. Students develop competencies required in the modern Zambian business environment.
LearningOutcomes: Produce clear and professional written business documents including reports and correspondence
Demonstrate effective oral communication skills in presentations and meetings
Apply appropriate communication strategies across different business contexts and audiences

Description: A foundational course in financial and management accounting, covering the recording, classification, and analysis of financial transactions for business decision-making. Topics include the accounting cycle, ledgers, trial balance, and preparation of basic financial statements.
LearningOutcomes: Record and classify financial transactions using double-entry bookkeeping
Prepare basic financial statements including income statements and balance sheets
Interpret financial data to support business planning and management decisions

Description: An elective course exploring entrepreneurial thinking and innovation management, guiding students through the process of identifying business opportunities and developing viable ventures. Special emphasis is placed on the challenges and opportunities facing SMEs in Zambia.
LearningOutcomes: Identify and evaluate entrepreneurial opportunities in local and regional markets
Develop a comprehensive business plan incorporating innovation strategies
Analyse the challenges and opportunities facing small and medium enterprises in Zambia

Description: A foundational course in biological sciences covering cell biology, genetics, ecology, and the diversity of life, with an emphasis on local ecosystems and biodiversity in Zambia. Laboratory sessions introduce students to standard biological techniques.
LearningOutcomes: Describe the fundamental principles of cell biology, genetics, and evolution
Identify major taxonomic groups of organisms and their ecological roles in Zambian ecosystems
Conduct basic biological laboratory techniques including microscopy and specimen preparation

Description: An intermediate chemistry course covering organic and inorganic chemistry principles, chemical reactions, stoichiometry, and laboratory techniques relevant to natural science disciplines. Students gain practical skills in chemical analysis and safety.
LearningOutcomes: Explain fundamental concepts of organic and inorganic chemistry including atomic structure and bonding
Perform quantitative chemical analysis using standard laboratory methods
Apply chemical principles to interpret natural phenomena and environmental processes

Description: An elective course examining environmental systems, human impacts on natural ecosystems, and sustainable development strategies. Strong focus on environmental challenges unique to the Copperbelt region, including mining pollution, land degradation, and water quality issues.
LearningOutcomes: Analyse the interactions between human activities and natural environmental systems
Assess the environmental impact of mining and industrial activities in the Copperbelt region
Propose evidence-based solutions for environmental conservation and sustainable resource management
